source.basis: Operator spec page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
CyrusOne CIN6 publishes 5 MW of IT capacity across 143,000 square feet of technical space in Florence, Kentucky. At 10 kW per rack, a common colocation density, 5 MW supports roughly 500 racks; at 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density, the same 5 MW supports roughly 125 racks. Those are assumptions about density, not the operator's claim. The ratio of technical space to power, about 28,600 square feet per megawatt, suggests the floor was designed for moderate rather than high-density compute, though the operator publishes no rack-count or power-density figure that would settle the question.

The certifications qualify this campus to host payment card data under PCI DSS, protected health information under HIPAA, federal information systems under FISMA, and general enterprise workloads under ISO 27001 and SSAE 16 Type II audit. Green Globes indicates a third-party environmental performance assessment of the building. No certification speaks directly to AI workloads, and no tenant information is published.

Within Kentucky, this site ranks first by published IT capacity, but that ranking reflects limited data: of five facilities mapped in the state, only one, this campus, has published a megawatt figure. The state's total published capacity is therefore exactly 5 MW, all of it attributable to CIN6. Kentucky is not among the states with large concentrations of AI-oriented capacity, and at 5 MW this campus is small relative to hyperscale AI campuses that now routinely publish figures above 100 MW. CIN6 is a regional enterprise colocation facility, not a primary destination for large-scale AI training infrastructure as the numbers currently stand.
